content: 1. Zanamivir has been studied for its effectiveness in preventing the progression of influenza, as referenced in the NAIB2006 report accessed on August 7, 2024. 2. Boltz DA, Rehg JE, McClaren J, Webster RG, and Govorkova EA conducted research demonstrating that oseltamivir prophylactic regimens effectively prevent morbidity and mortality associated with H5N1 influenza in a ferret model. This study was published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2008 (Volume 197, Pages 1315–1323). 3. Sahakyan YS evaluated the impact of point-of-care diagnostic tests for influenza on health outcomes using a decision-analytic model, as detailed in a referenced PDF. 4. Steinberg E, Greenfield S, Wolman DM, Mancher M, and Graham R authored a publication titled Clinical Practice Guidelines We Can Trust, released by the National Academies Press in 2011. 5. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Schunemann HJ, Tugwell P, and Knottnerus A introduced the GRADE guidelines in a series of articles published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011 (Volume 64, Pages 380–382). 6. Guyatt G, Oxman AD, Akl EA, Kunz R, Vist G, Brozek J, and colleagues provided an introduction to GRADE evidence profiles and summary of findings tables in the first article of the GRADE guidelines series, published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011 (Volume 64, Pages 383–394). 7. Saleem N, Kulkarni A, Snow TAC, Ambler G, Singer M, and Arulkumaran N conducted a systematic review, meta-analysis, and meta-regression of randomized controlled trials to assess the effect of corticosteroids on mortality and clinical cure in community-acquired pneumonia. Their findings were published in Chest in 2023 (Volume 163, Pages 484–497). 8. Schunemann HJ and Guyatt GH provided a commentary titled Goodbye M(C)ID. Hello MID, where do you come from? in Health Services Research in 2005 (Volume 40, Pages 593–597). The article is available through PubMed Central (PMC1361157).
